Dark tapering brush outline, flat even ink-wash fill, uniform ambient tone with no visible light source, no cast shadow, no sheen. Monochromatic warm grey from pale paper to near-black ink. Brush character at every edge.

Subject: the BACK VIEW of the swordsman in the first image, seen from directly behind, as the matching view on a character turnaround sheet. Exactly the same man, same size in frame, same upright symmetrical stance, feet shoulder-width apart, both arms straight and held away from the body at the same angle, hands open and empty. Back of the wide conical straw hat, back of the blue-grey robe with its frayed hem and ragged sleeve ends, dark cloth wraps on forearms and lower legs, straw sandals seen from behind. ONE sword in a dark scabbard slung diagonally across his back: the wrapped hilt rises above his right shoulder (now on the viewer's right) and the scabbard tip ends near his left hip (the viewer's left). The two tan gourds hang at his left hip (the viewer's left). The second image shows the same man from behind in the original painting: take the look of his back, the sword and the robe from it, but keep the pose and proportions of the first image.

Plain empty paper background and nothing else in the picture: no ground line, no cliff wall, no mist, no clouds, no shadow, no text, no seal. Whole subject in frame with a paper margin all round.
